      (a) point-based backbone                   (b) voxel-based backbone                             (c) the proposed voxel-point interaction backbone

Figure 1. (a) The mainstream point-based 3D VG backbone. The point cloud needs to be downsampled aggressively from the original
50,000 points directly to 2,048 points. (b) The voxel-based backbone TSP3D-B [12]. The voxels can be progressively downsampled but the
number of voxels grows almost exponentially in the upsampling stage, which hinders efficient interaction with the textual semantics. (c)
The proposed PV-Ground combines the advantages from both sides. It maintains the integrity of scene representation through progressive
sparse voxel convolution, while is also efficient to interact with textual queries through a small amount of compact keypoint features.

Figure 2. An illustration of PV-Ground. The raw point cloud is voxelized and fed into multi-layer sparse convolutions to form a voxel
feature pyramid. We designed a text-guided keypoint sampling module to obtain target-relevant keypoints from the scene. Each keypoint
aggregates multi-scale features from the neighbor voxel feature pyramid, thereby converting the large voxel features into a compact keypoint
feature representation. The grounding/segmentation results is predicted by interacting these keypoints with the text.

3.1. Overview of the Proposed Framework                                           tailed as follows.
The proposed PV-Ground framework uniquely integrates a                            Voxel Convolution. Sparse voxel convolution can offer
voxel-based backbone with a keypoint-based aggregation                            higher resolution and provide more detailed 3D scene data
and interaction mechanism. The core objective is to lever-                        while maintaining high inference speed, making it highly
age the high-resolution, fine-grained features from sparse                        efficient and accurate for 3D scene feature extraction. The
voxel convolutions while retaining the computational con-                         model input is P ∈ RN ×6 , representing a point cloud of N
venience of keypoint-based multi-modal fusion.                                    points, where each point has six-dimensional features (XYZ
    The overall architecture is illustrated in Figure 2. The                      and RGB). First, we voxelize the input point cloud into a
raw input point cloud is first voxelized and then processed                       Lv × Wv × Hv voxel grid representation. The voxel fea-
by sparse voxel convolutions to generate a multi-scale voxel                      tures are then fed into a sparse voxel convolution network
feature pyramid. This preserves rich geometric and contex-                        as shown in Figure 2. Each convolutional block downsam-
tual details that are often lost in point-based downsampling.                     ples the voxel feature maps with a stride of 2, ultimately
Next, a voxel-to-keypoint feature aggregation mechanism                           forming a voxel feature pyramid. To supplement the con-
is designed to distill the large-scale voxel feature pyramid                      volutional features, the 8× downsampled feature maps are
into compact, target-aware keypoints. This compact repre-                         stacked along the Z-axis to form a BEV (Bird’s Eye View)
sentation, which is both high-fidelity (derived from voxels)                      feature map, completing the multi-scale voxel feature pyra-
and text-focused (guided by TGS), is then fed into a multi-                       mid. This voxel-based representation provides a rich, hier-
modal interaction module for deep interaction with the text                       archical representation of the scene, from fine-grained local
embeddings encoded by the pre-trained RoBERTa [23]. Fi-                           details to high-level contextual semantics.
nally, a task head performs object localization and segmen-                       Voxel-to-Keypoint Feature Interaction. Directly using

parentheses. PV-Ground outperforms the baseline model by over 5% and over 2% in the single-stage and two-stage pipelines, respectively.
